method: Every row was compared with both readings side by side: the exact crop enlarged above the chart cards for the proposed codes, the number field cropped from the original page, and a boundary test of the crop box against the connected ink of the page at 600 dpi. Where the readers agreed, the shared reading was checked against these views and kept; where they disagreed, the disputed unit was enlarged next to the candidate cards and, for stroke groups, ticks and hatched patches, measured on the page raster (8.3 px per point) and compared with the same measurement of the printed sign list on PDF pages 20 and 21. No set was made unique by intersecting the readings. Coincident cards and the 144/244 pair stay together in the strict set; a unit that no card matches has an empty strict set with the reason in its note.

policy.code_vocabulary: position-chart card labels, as the conventions direct; composite labels contribute every listed code
policy.strict_candidate_codes: cards whose drawing, underline state and cell placement all agree with the source; coincident cards stay together
policy.shape_only_candidate_codes: strict codes plus cards that agree after ignoring underline or cell placement, and alternatives either reader named unless the source excluded them
policy.crop_correct: true only when the box contains all drawing and underline ink and no neighbour or field ink; crop_issues are filled for every false crop, crop_observations hold remarks on accepted crops
policy.narrow_hatched_patches: the patch edge facing the neighbouring sign decides between 597/13 (left edge) and 598/542 (right edge): the patch ink lies 1.6 to 2.3 pt from the neighbouring cell, or about 5 pt from the neighbour ink, whichever the neighbour allows; the opposite edge would leave about 8 pt more. All 16 patch units were measured at 600 dpi (values in the unit notes) and agree with both readers.
policy.two_column_patch_762: rows 14 and 20 show two patch columns 2.52 pt apart; card 762 holds two columns 2.40 pt apart in one cell, whereas two abutting patch cells would show the 1.6 to 2.3 pt inter-cell gap. Read as one unit; the two-unit count is kept as an alternative.

Reader B chose 765 from spacings of 4.1 and 4.4 pt measured on the 3.95 px/pt chart cards, a difference that the native-resolution measurement does not reproduce.
Same measurement as row 8 unit 5: source spacing 4.07 pt against card spacings 4.2 pt (9) and 4.1 pt (765); the set is kept.

The source figure has a horizontal bar with a triangular flap hanging at each end and a plain stem above. Card 143 shows that. Card 341 has a triangular apex above the figure, which the source does not have.

The source is a fish with a double chevron above the body. Reader B wrote chart location 20:2:28 beside its code 36, and 20:2:28 is the card labelled 86; card 36 (21:1:6) is a double bow-tie. The code 36 is a slip for 86.
The source U has the F-shaped flag on both arms and a five-dash underline (visible in the zoomed crop). Card 526 is the underlined U with flags; card 548 is a plain underlined U with no flag.

Card 350 (21:1:19) is a bow-tie with the right vertical complete and the left vertical reduced to top and bottom ticks, which is the drawing in the source (no underline). Reader A compared only with 241 and 234 and did not find it. Card 793 is the underlined twin and stays in the shape-only set.

The source figure has no triangle and no dots between the legs, so card 144 is the plain match. The conventions tell the adjudicator to preserve the documented 144/244 labelling uncertainty as a source observation; both codes therefore stay in the strict set. Reader A put 244 in the shape-only list, which does not preserve that uncertainty.
Zoomed source shows a third prong rising between the two arms of the Y. Card 126 has that prong; card 443 is a plain two-armed Y.

The source has four strokes. Card 767 has four strokes; card 12 (20:7:21) has five on the chart and in the printed sign list. Reader B described the cards as coincident, but card 12 does not match the stroke count. The underlined four-stroke cards 294 and 771 are shape-only candidates.

The source tick is one continuous stroke 2.4 pt long at the top of the line, no underline. Card 23 is printed as a dot above a 1.4 pt stroke with a 0.5 pt gap (2.2 pt in all), which the source does not show; card 258 has the same long high stroke but is underlined; card 1 is a centred tick. No card matches all properties, so the strict set is empty (reader A) and 1, 23, 258 are shape-only candidates.

Two ink components of 5 and 2 pixels at 600 dpi cross the bottom edge of the box; they belong to the tips of the next numbered line. The convention requires a correct crop to exclude neighbour ink; rows 44, 48, 55, 58 and 66 are rejected for the same reason with more ink.

Both readers chose card 23 for an isolated high tick. The source tick (row 35 unit 2) is one continuous stroke 2.2 pt long with no underline; native-resolution measurement of the printed sign list shows card 23 as a dot above a 1.4 pt stroke with a gap, and card 258 as a continuous 2.3 pt high stroke with an underline. The shared reading is replaced by an empty strict set with shape-only 1, 23, 258, the same treatment as row 70 unit 4.
